historical_references.reference: The name Shashwat is a Sanskrit word which means eternal, infinite, or enduring. It is a common name in Hindu mythology and is also used as a title for various gods and goddesses. One such deity is Shashwat Muni, a sage who is believed to have a boon of immortality.

Another reference to the name Shashwat can be found in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic. In this text, the character Bhishma Pitamaha is referred to as Shashwat, as he is believed to have the power to choose the time of his own death. His name signifies his ability to remain eternal in spirit.
